User message:
I have only noticed this on mobile (mobile Chrome pwa) but it's a huge bug 

When the agent is asking a question that we need to show a form for, to choose from available options - that form keeps appearing and disappearing. It probably shows for about a second and then it disappears for about 4 or 5 seconds, then it comes back for a second, and on and on again and again. 

You must fix this and fix this forever. 

It might be related to another bug, which is that sometimes, in fact anytime that there's an agent working and producing output, even if not in the same session, there is a crazy lag for typing in the input box

```text
1	import type { WorkerEntry } from "@/shared/worker-entries";
2	
3	export type PendingWorkerElicitation = {
4	  requestId: number;
5	  requestedAt: string;
6	  sessionId?: string | null;
7	  toolCallId?: string | null;
8	  mode?: "form" | "url" | null;
9	  elicitationId?: string | null;
10	  url?: string | null;
11	  message?: string | null;
12	  requestedSchema?: {
13	    type?: string;
14	    properties?: Record<string, unknown>;
15	    required?: string[];
16	  } | null;
17	};
18	
19	const TERMINAL_ELICITATION_STATUSES = new Set([
20	  "answered",
21	  "cancelled",
22	  "canceled",
23	  "completed",
24	  "declined",
25	  "failed",
26	  "rejected",
27	  "skipped",
28	]);
29	
30	function asRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
31	  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
32	    ? value as Record<string, unknown>
33	    : null;
34	}
35	
36	function asString(value: unknown): string | null {
37	  return typeof value === "string" ? value : null;
38	}
39	
40	function asRequestedSchema(value: unknown): PendingWorkerElicitation["requestedSchema"] {
41	  const schema = asRecord(value);
42	  if (!schema) {
43	    return null;
44	  }
45	  const properties = asRecord(schema.properties) ?? {};
46	  const required = Array.isArray(schema.required)
47	    ? schema.required.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === "string")
48	    : undefined;
49	  const type = asString(schema.type);
50	  return {
51	    properties,
52	    ...(type ? { type } : {}),
53	    ...(required ? { required } : {}),
54	  };
55	}
56	
57	function normalizeElicitationStatus(entry: WorkerEntry) {
58	  return (entry.status ?? "pending").trim().toLowerCase();
59	}
60	
61	function isOpenElicitationStatus(entry: WorkerEntry) {
62	  return !TERMINAL_ELICITATION_STATUSES.has(normalizeElicitationStatus(entry));
63	}
64	
65	function entryRequestId(entry: WorkerEntry) {
66	  const raw = asRecord(entry.raw);
67	  const requestId = raw?.requestId;
68	  return typeof requestId === "number" && Number.isFinite(requestId) ? requestId : null;
69	}
70	
71	function pendingFromEntry(entry: WorkerEntry): PendingWorkerElicitation | null {
72	  const raw = asRecord(entry.raw);
73	  const requestId = entryRequestId(entry);
74	  if (!raw || requestId === null || !isOpenElicitationStatus(entry)) {
75	    return null;
76	  }
77	  return {
78	    requestId,
79	    requestedAt: entry.timestamp,
80	    sessionId: asString(raw.sessionId),
81	    toolCallId: asString(raw.toolCallId ?? entry.toolCallId),
82	    mode: raw.mode === "form" || raw.mode === "url" ? raw.mode : null,
83	    elicitationId: asString(raw.elicitationId),
84	    url: asString(raw.url),
85	    message: asString(raw.message),
86	    requestedSchema: asRequestedSchema(raw.requestedSchema),
87	  };
88	}
89	
90	export function derivePendingElicitationsFromWorkerEntries(entries: readonly WorkerEntry[]): PendingWorkerElicitation[] {
91	  const pendingByRequestId = new Map<number, PendingWorkerElicitation>();
92	
93	  for (const entry of entries) {
94	    if (entry.type !== "elicitation") {
95	      continue;
96	    }
97	    const requestId = entryRequestId(entry);
98	    if (requestId === null) {
99	      continue;
100	    }
101	    if (!isOpenElicitationStatus(entry)) {
102	      pendingByRequestId.delete(requestId);
103	      continue;
104	    }
105	    const pending = pendingFromEntry(entry);
106	    if (pending) {
107	      pendingByRequestId.set(requestId, pending);
108	    }
109	  }
110	
111	  return Array.from(pendingByRequestId.values()).sort((left, right) => {
112	    const timeDelta = new Date(left.requestedAt).getTime() - new Date(right.requestedAt).getTime();
113	    return timeDelta || left.requestId - right.requestId;
114	  });
115	}
```

```text
export function applyStopWorkerOptimisticUpdate(
  current: EventStreamState,
  runId: string,
  workerId: string,
) {
  const now = new Date().toISOString();
  const run = current.runs.find((candidate) => candidate.id === runId) ?? null;
  const isImplementationRun = run?.mode === "implementation" && run?.phase !== "planning";
  const stoppedWorkerIds = new Set<string>();

  const workers = (current.workers || []).map((worker) => {
    if (worker.runId !== runId) {
      return worker;
    }
    if (
      worker.id === workerId
      || (isImplementationRun && isOptimisticallyStoppableWorkerStatus(worker.status))
    ) {
      stoppedWorkerIds.add(worker.id);
      return { ...worker, status: "cancelled", updatedAt: now };
    }
    return worker;
  });

export function applyElicitationOptimisticUpdate(
  current: EventStreamState,
  workerId: string,
  requestId: number,
) {
  return {
    ...current,
    agents: (current.agents || []).map((agent) =>
      agent.name === workerId
        ? {
            ...agent,
            pendingElicitations: (agent.pendingElicitations || [])
              .filter((elicitation) => elicitation.requestId !== requestId),
          }
        : agent),
  };
}

export function isAlreadyResolvedHumanInputError(error: unknown) {
  const descriptor = buildInlineError(error);
  return descriptor.status === 409
    || /\bno_pending_(?:elicitations|permissions)\b/i.test(descriptor.message);
}
```

```text
79	  setMobileSettingsOpen = (mobileSettingsOpen: boolean) => this.setKey("mobileSettingsOpen", mobileSettingsOpen);

81	
82	const composerUiManager = new ComposerUiManager();
83	
84	function ConversationComposerInner({
```

```text
1	"use client";
2	
3	import { useCallback, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
4	import type { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";
5	
6	export function useManagerSnapshot<TState>(manager: StateManager<TState>) {
7	  return useSyncExternalStore(
8	    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
9	    useCallback(() => manager.getSnapshot(), [manager]),
10	    useCallback(() => manager.getInitialSnapshot(), [manager]),
11	  );
12	}
13	
14	export function shallowEqualRecord<TRecord extends Record<string, unknown>>(
15	  left: TRecord,
16	  right: TRecord,
17	) {
18	  if (Object.is(left, right)) {
19	    return true;
20	  }
21	
22	  const leftKeys = Object.keys(left);
23	  const rightKeys = Object.keys(right);
24	  if (leftKeys.length !== rightKeys.length) {
25	    return false;
26	  }
27	
28	  return leftKeys.every((key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(right, key)
29	    && Object.is(left[key], right[key]));
30	}
31	
32	export function useManagerSelector<TState, TSelected>(
33	  manager: StateManager<TState>,
34	  selector: (state: TState) => TSelected,
35	  isEqual: (left: TSelected, right: TSelected) => boolean = Object.is,
36	) {
37	  const selectionRef = useRef<{
38	    state: TState;
39	    selection: TSelected;
40	  } | null>(null);
41	  const serverSelectionRef = useRef<{
42	    state: TState;
43	    selector: (state: TState) => TSelected;
44	    selection: TSelected;
45	  } | null>(null);
46	
47	  const getSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
48	    const state = manager.getSnapshot();
49	    const previous = selectionRef.current;
50	    if (previous?.state === state) {
51	      return previous.selection;
52	    }
53	
54	    const nextSelection = selector(state);
55	    if (previous && isEqual(previous.selection, nextSelection)) {
56	      selectionRef.current = {
57	        state,
58	        selection: previous.selection,
59	      };
60	      return previous.selection;
61	    }
62	
63	    selectionRef.current = {
64	      state,
65	      selection: nextSelection,
66	    };
67	    return nextSelection;
68	  }, [isEqual, manager, selector]);
69	  const getServerSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
70	    const state = manager.getInitialSnapshot();
71	    const previous = serverSelectionRef.current;
72	    if (previous?.state === state && previous.selector === selector) {
73	      return previous.selection;
74	    }
75	    const selection = selector(state);
76	    serverSelectionRef.current = { state, selector, selection };
77	    return selection;
78	  }, [manager, selector]);
79	
80	  return useSyncExternalStore(
81	    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
82	    getSelectedSnapshot,
83	    getServerSelectedSnapshot,
84	  );
85	}
86
```

```text
1	export type StateUpdate<T> = T | ((current: T) => T);
2	export type StateListener = () => void;
3	
4	export class StateManager<TState> {
5	  private state: TState;
6	  private readonly initialState: TState;
7	  private readonly listeners = new Set<StateListener>();
8	
9	  constructor(initialState: TState) {
10	    this.state = initialState;
11	    this.initialState = initialState;
12	  }
13	
14	  getSnapshot() {
15	    return this.state;
16	  }
17	
18	  getInitialSnapshot() {
19	    return this.initialState;
20	  }
21	
22	  subscribe(listener: StateListener) {
23	    this.listeners.add(listener);
24	    return () => {
25	      this.listeners.delete(listener);
26	    };
27	  }
28	
29	  update(updater: StateUpdate<TState>, notify = true) {
30	    const nextState = typeof updater === "function"
31	      ? (updater as (current: TState) => TState)(this.state)
32	      : updater;
33	
34	    if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
35	      return this.state;
36	    }
37	
38	    this.state = nextState;
39	    if (notify) {
40	      this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
41	    }
42	    return this.state;
43	  }
44	
45	  patch(patch: Partial<TState> | ((current: TState) => Partial<TState>), notify = true) {
46	    return this.update((current) => ({
47	      ...current,
48	      ...(typeof patch === "function" ? patch(current) : patch),
49	    }), notify);
50	  }
51	
52	  setKey<TKey extends keyof TState>(key: TKey, value: StateUpdate<TState[TKey]>, notify = true) {
53	    return this.update((current) => {
54	      const nextValue = typeof value === "function"
55	        ? (value as (currentValue: TState[TKey]) => TState[TKey])(current[key])
56	        : value;
57	
58	      if (Object.is(nextValue, current[key])) {
59	        return current;
60	      }
61	
62	      return {
63	        ...current,
64	        [key]: nextValue,
65	      };
66	    }, notify);
67	  }
68	}
69
```

```text
193	          id: `${Date.now()}-${randomId}`,

204	
205	  addPastedImages(files: File[]) {
206	    this.addAttachmentFiles(files.map((file, index) => {
207	      if (file.name) {
208	        return file;
209	      }
210	
211	      const extension = file.type.split("/")[1]?.split(";")[0] || "png";
212	      return new File([file], `pasted-image-${Date.now()}-${index}.${extension}`, {
213	        type: file.type || "image/png",
214	        lastModified: file.lastModified || Date.now(),
215	      });
216	    }));
217	  }
218	
219	  removeAttachment(id: string) {
220	    this.setKey("attachments", (current) => {
221	      const removed = current.find((attachment) => attachment.id === id);
222	      if (removed) {
223	        this.revokeAttachmentPreview(removed);
224	      }
225	      return current.filter((attachment) => attachment.id !== id);
226	    });
227	  }
228	
229	  clearAttachments() {
230	    const current = this.getSnapshot().attachments;
231	    current.forEach((attachment) => this.revokeAttachmentPreview(attachment));
232	    this.setKey("attachments", []);
233	  }
234	
235	  setComposerDraft(patch: Partial<ComposerDraft>) {
236	    this.update((current) => {
237	      const command = patch.command ?? current.command;
238	      const commandCursor = patch.commandCursor ?? current.commandCursor;
239	      const mentionIndex = patch.mentionIndex ?? current.mentionIndex;
240	      const attachments = patch.attachments ?? current.attachments;
241	
242	      if (
243	        Object.is(command, current.command)
244	        && Object.is(commandCursor, current.commandCursor)
245	        && Object.is(mentionIndex, current.mentionIndex)
246	        && Object.is(attachments, current.attachments)
247	      ) {
248	        return current;
249	      }
250	
251	      return {
252	        ...current,
253	        command,
254	        commandCursor,
255	        mentionIndex,
256	        attachments,
257	      };
258	    });
259	  }
260	
261	  selectRun(nextRunId: string | null) {
262	    this.update((current) => {
263	      if (current.selectedRunId === nextRunId) return current;
264	      const prevKey = current.selectedRunId ?? NEW_CONVERSATION_DRAFT_KEY;
265	      const nextKey = nextRunId ?? NEW_CONVERSATION_DRAFT_KEY;
266	      const nextDraft = current.composerDraftsByRun[nextKey] ?? EMPTY_COMPOSER_DRAFT;
267	      const drafts: Record<string, ComposerDraft> = { ...current.composerDraftsByRun };
268	      const hasContent = current.command.length > 0
269	        || current.commandCursor !== 0
270	        || current.mentionIndex !== 0
271	        || current.attachments.length > 0;
272	      if (hasContent) {
273	        drafts[prevKey] = {
274	          command: current.command,
275	          commandCursor: current.commandCursor,
276	          mentionIndex: current.mentionIndex,
277	          attachments: current.attachments,
278	        };
279	      } else {
280	        delete drafts[prevKey];
281	      }
282	      if (nextDraft === EMPTY_COMPOSER_DRAFT) {
283	        delete drafts[nextKey];
284	      }
285	      return {
286	        ...current,
287	        selectedRunId: nextRunId,
288	        composerDraftsByRun: drafts,
289	        command: nextDraft.command,
290	        commandCursor: nextDraft.commandCursor,
291	        mentionIndex: nextDraft.mentionIndex,
292	        attachments: nextDraft.attachments,
293	      };
294	    });
295	  }
296	
297	  revealMoreProjectSessions(projectPath: string) {
298	    this.setKey("visibleProjectSessionCounts", (current) => ({
299	      ...current,
300	      [projectPath]: (current[projectPath] ?? PROJECT_SESSION_DISPLAY_BATCH_SIZE) + PROJECT_SESSION_DISPLAY_BATCH_SIZE,
301	    }));
302	  }
303	
304	  resetProjectSessionDisplayLimit(projectPath: string) {
305	    this.setKey("visibleProjectSessionCounts", (current) => {
306	      if (!(projectPath in current)) {
307	        return current;
308	      }
309	
310	      const next = { ...current };
311	      delete next[projectPath];
312	      return next;
313	    });
314	  }
315	
316	  setProjectExpanded(projectPath: string, expanded: boolean) {
317	    this.setKey("collapsedProjectPaths", (current) => {
318	      const next = new Set(current);
319	      if (expanded) {
320	        if (!next.has(projectPath)) return current;
321	        next.delete(projectPath);
322	      } else {
323	        if (next.has(projectPath)) return current;
324	        next.add(projectPath);
325	      }
326	      return next;
327	    });
328	  }
329	
330	  collapseProjects(projectPaths: string[]) {
331	    if (projectPaths.length === 0) return;
332	
333	    this.update((current) => {
334	      const collapsedProjectPaths = new Set(current.collapsedProjectPaths);
335	      let changed = false;
336	      for (const projectPath of projectPaths) {
337	        if (!collapsedProjectPaths.has(projectPath)) {
338	          collapsedProjectPaths.add(projectPath);
339	          changed = true;
340	        }
341	      }
342	
343	      if (!changed) return current;
344	
345	      const visibleProjectSessionCounts = { ...current.visibleProjectSessionCounts };
346	      for (const projectPath of projectPaths) {
347	        delete visibleProjectSessionCounts[projectPath];
348	      }
349	
350	      return {
351	        ...current,
352	        collapsedProjectPaths,
353	        visibleProjectSessionCounts,
354	      };
355	    });
356	  }
357	
358	  createSetter<TKey extends keyof HomeUiState>(key: TKey) {
359	    return (value: StateUpdate<HomeUiState[TKey]>) => {
360	      this.setKey(key, value);
361	    };
362	  }
363	}
```

```text
131	function hasRecoverErrorClearingEvent(events: ExecutionEventRecord[], submittedAt: number | undefined) {

133	    ? submittedAt

135	  return events.some((event) => {
136	    if (!RECOVER_ERROR_CLEARING_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.eventType)) {

143	    return eventTime !== null && eventTime >= submittedAtMs;
144	  });

154	function scopedMutationError(
```

```text
40	function timestampMs(value: string | null | undefined) {
41	  if (!value) return null;
42	  const time = new Date(value).getTime();
43	  return Number.isFinite(time) ? time : null;
44	}

46	function hasSuccessfulRecoveryAfterFailure(run: RunRecord, events: ExecutionEventRecord[]) {
47	  if (run.status !== "failed") {
48	    return false;
49	  }
50	
51	  const failureTime = timestampMs(run.failedAt ?? run.updatedAt ?? run.createdAt);
52	  if (failureTime === null) {
53	    return false;
54	  }
55	
56	  return events.some((event) => {
57	    if (!RECOVERY_SUCCESS_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.eventType)) {
58	      return false;
59	    }
60	    const eventTime = timestampMs(event.createdAt);
61	    return eventTime !== null && eventTime >= failureTime;
62	  });
63	}
```

```text
6	export type ConversationLoadState = {
7	  snapshotLoaded: boolean;
8	  workerStreamRequired: boolean;
9	  workerStreamLoaded: boolean;
10	  fullyLoaded: boolean;
11	  loadingReason: "snapshot" | "worker_stream" | null;
12	};
13	
14	export function isWorkerStreamCaughtUp(streamState: WorkerStreamState) {
15	  return (
16	    streamState.status === "loaded"
17	    && streamState.latestContiguousSeq === streamState.latestKnownSeq
18	  );
19	}
20	
21	export function deriveConversationLoadState(args: {
22	  snapshotLoaded: boolean;
23	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled: boolean;
24	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
25	  streamState: WorkerStreamState;
26	  selectedRunIsTerminal?: boolean;
27	}): ConversationLoadState {
28	  const workerStreamRequired = Boolean(
29	    args.unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled
30	      && args.primaryConversationWorkerId
31	      && !args.selectedRunIsTerminal
32	  );
33	  const workerStreamLoaded = !workerStreamRequired || isWorkerStreamCaughtUp(args.streamState);
34	  const fullyLoaded = args.snapshotLoaded && workerStreamLoaded;
35	  const loadingReason = !args.snapshotLoaded
36	    ? "snapshot"
37	    : !workerStreamLoaded
38	      ? "worker_stream"
39	      : null;
40	
41	  return {
42	    snapshotLoaded: args.snapshotLoaded,
43	    workerStreamRequired,
44	    workerStreamLoaded,
45	    fullyLoaded,
46	    loadingReason,
47	  };
48	}
49	
50	export function shouldShowDirectWorkerStreamInitialLoading(args: {
51	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled: boolean;
52	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
53	  streamState: WorkerStreamState;
54	}) {
55	  return deriveConversationLoadState({
56	    ...args,
57	    snapshotLoaded: true,
58	  }).loadingReason === "worker_stream"
59	    && (args.streamState.status === "idle" || args.streamState.status === "loading")
60	    && args.streamState.entries.length === 0;
61	}
62	
63	export function shouldShowDirectConversationLoading(args: ConversationLoadState) {
64	  return Boolean(
65	    !args.fullyLoaded
66	    && args.loadingReason === "worker_stream"
67	  );
68	}
69	
70	export function selectDirectConversationEntries<T extends WorkerEntry>(args: {
71	  transcriptEntries: T[];
72	  directWorkerEntries: T[];
73	  // Ranges the live worker wrote for a branch a retry/edit discarded. The
74	  // transcript already drops them server-side; the live stream is served from
75	  // the raw JSONL (no database read on that hot path), so they are filtered
76	  // here before the two sources are merged — otherwise the rewound turn walks
77	  // straight back into the conversation.
78	  supersededSeqRanges?: SupersededSeqRange[];
79	  // The run's workers in creation order, so a message that exists on more than
80	  // one of them is placed where the newest worker has it.
81	  workerOrder?: ReadonlyArray<string>;
82	}) {
83	  const directWorkerEntries = withoutSupersededEntries(
84	    args.directWorkerEntries,
85	    args.supersededSeqRanges ?? [],
86	  );
87	
88	  if (args.transcriptEntries.length === 0) {
89	    return directWorkerEntries;
90	  }
91	
92	  return coalesceWorkerEntriesById([
93	    ...args.transcriptEntries,
94	    ...directWorkerEntries,
95	  ], args.workerOrder ?? []) as T[];
96	}
97	
98	export function resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval(args: {
99	  unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled: boolean;
100	  primaryConversationWorkerId: string | null | undefined;
101	  activeRefreshIntervalMs: number;
102	  validationIntervalMs: number;
103	  showDirectControlWorkingIndicator: boolean;
104	  selectedRunIsTerminal?: boolean;
105	}) {
106	  if (!args.unifiedWorkerStreamEnabled || !args.primaryConversationWorkerId) {
107	    return null;
108	  }
109

111	    ? args.activeRefreshIntervalMs
112	    : args.validationIntervalMs;
113	}
```

```text
1	import { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";

4	export class AutoResumeExhaustionManager extends StateManager<Set<string>> {
5	  constructor() {
6	    super(new Set());
7	  }
8	
9	  clear(runId: string) {
10	    this.update((current) => {
11	      if (!current.has(runId)) return current;
12	      const next = new Set(current);
13	      next.delete(runId);
14	      return next;
15	    });
16	  }
17	
18	  mark(runId: string) {
19	    this.update((current) => {
20	      if (current.has(runId)) return current;
21	      return new Set(current).add(runId);
22	    });
23	  }
24	}
25	
26	export const autoResumeExhaustionManager = new AutoResumeExhaustionManager();
27	
28	export type HomeAppState = Omit<
29	  HomeUiState,

33	export function selectHomeAppState(state: HomeUiState): HomeAppState {
34	  const selected: Partial<HomeUiState> = { ...state };
35	  delete selected.command;
36	  delete selected.commandCursor;
37	  delete selected.mentionIndex;

42	function timestampMs(value: string | null | undefined) {
43	  if (!value) {
44	    return 0;
45	  }
46	  const parsed = new Date(value).getTime();
47	  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : 0;
48	}
49	
50	export function mergeReadMarkers(
51	  persisted: Record<string, string> | null | undefined,
52	  optimistic: Record<string, string>,
53	) {
54	  const merged = { ...(persisted ?? {}) };
55	  for (const [runId, readAt] of Object.entries(optimistic)) {
56	    if (timestampMs(readAt) >= timestampMs(merged[runId])) {
57	      merged[runId] = readAt;
58	    }
59	  }
60	  return merged;
61	}
```

````text
Perfect! Now I have enough information to provide a comprehensive bug report. Let me compile the findings:

## Bug Investigation Report: Composer Input Laggy During Agent Output

I've thoroughly investigated the message composer input lag that occurs whenever any agent is working—even in a different session. Here's the ranked list of concrete causes:

### Root Cause Analysis

**1. CRITICAL: Global Event Stream State Re-triggers Entire HomeApp Render Tree (lines 329-333, HomeApp.tsx)**

The `state` object (EventStreamState) is subscribed to without a selector in HomeApp:
```typescript
// /Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/HomeApp.tsx:329-333
const state = useSyncExternalStore(
  useCallback((listener) => stateManager.subscribe(listener), [stateManager]),
  useCallback(() => stateManager.getSnapshot(), [stateManager]),
  () => initialEventState,
);
```

This `state` dependency flows through to `vm` (useHomeViewModel) at line 481, which has **multiple `useMemo` hooks** that depend on **entire array properties** rather than fine-grained selectors:

- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/useHomeViewModel.ts:220-230`: `activeProjects` depends on `state.messages, state.workers, state.agents, state.queuedMessages` (not individual items)
- Line 235-237: `selectedRunMessages` depends on `state.messages`  
- Line 251-257: `filteredMessages` depends on `state.messages`
- Line 263-265: `selectedRunWorkers` depends on `state.workers`
- Line 297: `conversationAgents` depends on `state.agents`

Every agent output event chunk triggers `EventStreamStateManager.update()` at line 324 (EventStreamStateManager.ts), which calls `listener(this.state)` for all subscribers. This creates a **new state object reference**, invalidating all these `useMemo` dependencies even when the compositor subscribes via `useManagerSelector` with a selector that excludes draft state.

**Impact**: Every single keystroke causes a full re-evaluation of sidebar filtering, conversation agents, and message lists.

---

**2. HIGH: No Selector on `state` Reference in HomeApp (lines 329-333, 480-493)**

Unlike the composer which uses `useManagerSelector(homeUiStateManager, selectHomeAppState, shallowEqualRecord)` at line 254, the event stream state has **no selector**. It should use a selector that only returns properties relevant to the current view:

```typescript
// Current (WRONG):
const state = useSyncExternalStore(
  useCallback((listener) => stateManager.subscribe(listener), [stateManager]),
  useCallback(() => stateManager.getSnapshot(), [stateManager]),
  () => initialEventState,
);

// Should be (with selector):
const state = useManagerSelector(stateManager, selectRelevantEventStreamState, deepEqualityCheck);
```

**File:Line**: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/HomeApp.tsx:329-333`

---

**3. HIGH: Array Equality Always False on Every Event (useHomeViewModel.ts deps)**

In `useHomeViewModel.ts`, the dependencies array references **entire arrays**:
- `state.messages` 
- `state.workers`
- `state.agents`
- `state.queuedMessages`

Because `EventStreamStateManager` creates new arrays via spread operations (e.g., `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/EventStreamStateManager.ts:157-160` in `mergeScopedMessages`), the arrays are never reference-equal, so `useMemo` never hits and re-computes on every event chunk.

**Files:Lines**:
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/useHomeViewModel.ts:220-230` (activeProjects)
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/useHomeViewModel.ts:235-237` (selectedRunMessages)
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/useHomeViewModel.ts:251-257` (filteredMessages)

---

**4. MEDIUM: Terminal Component Rebuilds Activity List on Every Event Chunk**

The Terminal component rebuilds activity from entries on every `entries` prop change:
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/Terminal.tsx:2210-2271` in `activity` useMemo depends on `entries`, which changes whenever `state.executionEvents` or `state.workers` are updated in a parent.
- The `buildAgentOutputActivity()` call at line 2261 parses and sorts all entries on every keystroke in another session.

**File:Line**: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/Terminal.tsx:2210-2271`

---

**5. MEDIUM: No Event Batching in LiveEventConnectionManager**

SSE events are applied immediately one-by-one to state:
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:240-241`: Each `"update"` event calls `this.handleUpdateEvent()` synchronously
- Line 276: `this.applyUpdate(data)` fires listeners immediately for each chunk

There's no batching of incoming event chunks into a single render flush.

**File:Lines**: 
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/LiveEventConnectionManager.ts:240-276`

---

**6. MEDIUM: EventStreamStateManager Creates New Object References on Every Update**

In `EventStreamStateManager.update()` (line 305-326), the new state is **always a fresh object**:
```typescript
// /Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/EventStreamStateManager.ts:313-316
const nextState = {
  ...mergeScopedMessages(this.state, incomingWithRuns),
  snapshotSource,
};
```

This guarantees that even if messages/workers/agents arrays are unchanged, the top-level state object is new, triggering re-subscriptions.

**File:Line**: `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/EventStreamStateManager.ts:313-326`

---

### Shared Root Cause: Elicitation Form Flicker

The elicitation form flicker bug shares the same root cause as composer lag. The `workerCardManager` (holding elicitation open state) at `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/component-state-managers.ts:250-265` and the global event stream both update on every agent output chunk. When the event stream mutates and triggers re-renders across the sidebar, the elicitation UI state briefly becomes inconsistent, causing the form to toggle open/closed.

---

### Summary Ranked by Impact

1. **Critical**: HomeApp subscribes to full event stream state without selector → every chunk re-renders entire tree including composer
2. **High**: useHomeViewModel has unselectorized array dependencies → O(n) message/worker/agent list filtering runs per chunk
3. **High**: EventStreamStateManager creates new state objects on every update → breaks memoization
4. **Medium**: Terminal rebuilds activity list on every event chunk (includes sorting/parsing)
5. **Medium**: No event batching in LiveEventConnectionManager → each SSE frame triggers separate state update
6. **Medium**: Elicitation UI uses separate state manager, conflicting with event stream updates → causes flicker
````

```text
2	 * Single source of truth for the unified worker conversation stream on
3	 * the frontend.
4	 *
5	 * Per (workerId) we hold a contiguous *window* [lowestSeq..latestContiguousSeq]:
6	 *   - entries: the contiguous window in seq order, never with gaps.
7	 *   - lowestSeq: the lowest seq currently in `entries` (0 if empty).
8	 *   - latestContiguousSeq: the highest seq we have proven contiguous
9	 *     from lowestSeq. Used as the cursor for forward refetch.
10	 *   - latestKnownSeq: the highest seq the server has told us exists.
11	 *     Updates immediately on a wake-up frame; the fetch fills the gap.
12	 *   - hasOlder: true if older entries exist on the server before
13	 *     lowestSeq. Set by initial tail-load and `loadOlder`.
14	 *   - status: "idle" → "loading" → "loaded"; "error" on a fetch failure.
15	 *
16	 * Initial load fetches the last N entries via `?limit=N`. Forward
17	 * extension uses `?afterSeq=latestContiguousSeq`. Backward hydration
18	 * uses `?beforeSeq=lowestSeq&limit=N` via `loadOlder`.
19	 *
20	 * SSE frames carry only `{ workerId, seq }` — the content is fetched
21	 * via the HTTP endpoint. The frame is a wake-up hint; we never trust
22	 * it as the entry payload.
23	 */
24	import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";

29	/**
30	 * Collapse multiple rows that share an entry `id` into a single
31	 * conversation item. The server's unified stream intentionally appends
32	 * a new row whenever an entry's text grows (so a streaming assistant
33	 * message can be revised in place — see the
34	 * `appends changed bridge message revisions so streaming prose can expand`
35	 * test in `tests/server/workers/output-store.test.ts`). It also
36	 * writes the same user_input id onto a newer worker's stream when a run
37	 * cycles through workers.
38	 *
39	 * Coalesce policy:
40	 *   - Keep the entry at its FIRST appearance in the input order, so
41	 *     conversational position doesn't jump when text grows.
42	 *   - Use the LATEST revision's text / metadata (text grows; latest
43	 *     revision is the finished one).
44	 *   - Take the timestamp from the copy on the NEWEST worker, because that
45	 *     is the one the live thread actually contains. Neither "earliest" nor
46	 *     "latest" works on its own: a rewind re-delivers a message with a new
47	 *     timestamp (newest is right, earliest pins it back above output it was
48	 *     rewound past), while `reconcileWorkerUserMessagesInStream` backfills
49	 *     history onto a fresh worker with the original `createdAt` (earliest is
50	 *     right, latest drags the opening prompt into the middle of the day).
51	 *     Worker order settles both. Copies from the same worker — streaming
52	 *     revisions, which share a timestamp anyway — keep the earliest.
53	 *   - Entries without an id pass through unchanged.
54	 *
55	 * `workerOrder` is the run's workers in creation order. Without it (a single
56	 * worker stream, or a caller that has no worker list yet) the earliest
57	 * timestamp is kept, which is the conservative choice: a message stays where
58	 * it already is.
59	 */
60	export function coalesceWorkerEntriesById(
61	  entries: ReadonlyArray<WorkerEntry>,
62	  workerOrder: ReadonlyArray<string> = [],
63	): WorkerEntry[] {
64	  const workerRank = new Map(workerOrder.map((workerId, index) => [workerId, index]));
65	  const rankOf = (entry: WorkerEntry) => {
66	    const workerId = (entry as { workerId?: unknown }).workerId;
67	    return typeof workerId === "string" ? workerRank.get(workerId) ?? -1 : -1;
68	  };
69	
70	  const positionByKey = new Map<string, number>();
71	  const placementByKey = new Map<string, { timestamp: string; rank: number }>();
72	  const result: WorkerEntry[] = [];
73	  for (const entry of entries) {
74	    const key = typeof entry.id === "string" && entry.id ? entry.id : null;
75	    if (!key) {
76	      result.push(entry);
77	      continue;
78	    }
79	    const existingPosition = positionByKey.get(key);
80	    if (existingPosition === undefined) {
81	      positionByKey.set(key, result.length);
82	      if (entry.timestamp) {

91	      if (held && candidate) {

107	      result[existingPosition] = { ...entry, timestamp: preservedTimestamp };
108	    }
109	  }
110	  return result;
111	}
```

````text
Perfect! Now I have the full picture. Let me compile my findings:

## PRECISE CAUSAL EXPLANATION OF THE FLICKERING BUG

I've traced both input sources thoroughly. Here's the exact race condition causing the ~1s visible / ~4-5s gone flickering cycle:

### **ROOT CAUSE: Race Between Two Polling Cycles With Different Update Frequencies**

#### **(A) Primary Source: `primaryConversationAgent.pendingElicitations` (Agent Snapshots)**

**Data Flow:**
- ConversationMain.tsx:1136 renders `InlineElicitation` if `pendingElicitations[0]` is truthy
- pendingElicitations is computed in ConversationMain.tsx:901-909
- It pulls from `primaryConversationAgent?.pendingElicitations ?? []` (line 902)
- primaryConversationAgent comes from useHomeViewModel, line 305, via `selectPrimaryConversationAgent(conversationAgents, isDirectConversation)`
- conversationAgents comes from state.agents (useHomeViewModel.ts:267-297)
- state.agents is populated via EventStreamStateManager from LiveEventConnectionManager
- LiveEventConnectionManager fetches agent snapshots via the SSE stream at `/api/events`

**Server-side Agent Snapshot Generation:**
- `/api/events` calls `buildRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload` (events.ts:645-731)
- This makes an HTTP request to `BRIDGE_URL/agents` with a 5-second timeout (events.ts:658, RUNTIME_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 at line 44)
- **CRITICAL**: In buildLiveWorkerSnapshot (live-snapshots.ts:171-236), line 215 **zeros out pendingElicitations when the run is terminal**:
  ```
  pendingElicitations: terminalRun ? [] : normalizedAgent.pendingElicitations
  ```
  where `terminalRun` is defined at line 193 and determined by isTerminalRun (line 145-153)

**Polling Intervals:**
- SSE stream polls for updated agent snapshots every STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000ms (15 seconds) (events.ts:42)
- But there's a RUNTIME_AGENT_GRACE_MS = 150ms (events.ts:43) race: if the bridge fetch takes longer than 150ms, the client is sent the *persisted* snapshot (without live agents) first, then the runtime-enriched snapshot arrives later
- The SSE loop (events.ts:954-1001) tries to fetch runtime payload with a 150ms grace period, falls back to persisted, then sends the enriched version if it arrives

**The Problem with Terminal Runs:**
- If the run's status changes to "done"/"failed"/"cancelled" (line 147-152), isTerminalRun returns true
- This causes pendingElicitations to be hardcoded to `[]` in line 215, **even if the agent still has pending elicitations server-side**
- The run status is fetched from the database and included in the snapshot

#### **(B) Secondary Source: `directWorkerStream.entries` (Worker Entry Stream)**

**Data Flow:**
- ConversationMain.tsx:852-865 calls `useWorkerStream` to load worker entries
- useWorkerStream (WorkerEntriesManager.ts:791-835) manages a sliding window of entries
- Entries are loaded via `refresh()` (line 378) which calls `fetchForward()` (line 565)
- **CRITICAL**: Initial load fetches the last DEFAULT_TAIL_LIMIT = 100 entries (line 118, 279-280)
- When cached entries exceed 100, they're sliced to the tail: `rawNextEntries.slice(-DEFAULT_TAIL_LIMIT)` (WorkerEntriesManager.ts:279-280)

**Polling Intervals:**
- useWorkerStream sets up a polling interval at ConversationMain.tsx:856-863
- The interval is resolved by `resolveDirectWorkerStreamRefreshInterval` (direct-worker-stream-loading.ts:98-113)
- Returns either activeRefreshIntervalMs (2 seconds) or validationIntervalMs (5 seconds) depending on whether a worker is active
- ConversationMain.tsx line 54-55 defines:
  ```
  const DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 2_000;
  const DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000;
  ```

**The Window Sliding Problem:**
- The elicitation entry (with type="elicitation") enters the 100-entry sliding window at fetch time
- If the worker stream has many entries, a 2s refresh cycle will eventually scroll the original elicitation entry *past* the tail window (entries 1-100)
- When that happens, `derivePendingElicitationsFromWorkerEntries` (worker-elicitations.ts:90-115) no longer finds the entry and returns an empty array
- The entry must have:
  - type = "elicitation" (line 94)
  - raw.requestId must exist (line 97-98)
  - Status must be open (not in TERMINAL_ELICITATION_STATUSES, line 61-63, 19-28)

#### **THE FLICKERING CYCLE: ~1s visible, ~4-5s gone, repeating**

**Timing Analysis:**

1. **Minute 0: Elicitation enters worker stream**
   - Fetch loads 100 tail entries, includes the elicitation entry (seq N)
   - Agent snapshot includes pendingElicitations from bridge
   - `pendingElicitations[0]` is truthy → InlineElicitation renders (visible)

2. **Minute ~2s: First refresh cycle (2s interval from line 54)**
   - Worker entries refresh via `refresh()` → `fetchForward()` (WorkerEntriesManager.ts:378-380)
   - New entries (seq N+1, N+2, ...) arrive and are appended
   - Total entries now exceed 100
   - On next state update: entries are sliced to last 100, **elicitation entry (seq N) scrolls out**
   - `derivePendingElicitationsFromWorkerEntries` no longer finds the elicitation
   - Combined list becomes empty → form disappears (~gone phase starts)

3. **Minute ~5s: Agent snapshot refresh cycle (15s SSE, but also captured by 5s validation interval)**
   - events.ts line 993: `waitForEventStreamNotification(STREAM_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS, notificationVersionAtStart)`
   - But validation happens every 5s (line 55: DIRECT_WORKER_STREAM_VALIDATION_INTERVAL_MS)
   - Agent snapshot is fetched fresh from bridge (if run isn't terminal)
   - `primaryConversationAgent.pendingElicitations` is now repopulated from live bridge state
   - Combined list has entry again → form reappears (~visible phase starts)

4. **Minute ~7s: Next 2s worker stream refresh**
   - Same as step 2 repeats
   - Elicitation scrolls out of the 100-entry window again
   - Form disappears

5. **Cycle repeats every ~5-7s**

**Mobile/PWA Specifics:**
- Mobile Chrome PWA has tighter memory constraints and may hit the 100-entry window limit more frequently
- The validation interval (5s) may sync with the active refresh (2s) on mobile, creating a 5-7s cycle pattern
- No visibility/pagehide handlers reset state on their own, but the window-sliding logic is the culprit

### **KEY ISSUE: Two Mismatched Time Scales**

- Worker entries refresh every **2 seconds** with a **100-entry sliding window**
- Agent snapshots refresh every **5-15 seconds** from the bridge
- On fast/streaming workers, the 100-entry window fills in ~2-10 seconds, causing the elicitation to scroll out
- The agent snapshot arrives 5-7 seconds after the window scrolls, making the form flicker on/off

### **File:Line Citations:**

**Problem A (Agent zeroing):**
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/workers/live-snapshots.ts:215` - pending elicitations zeroed for terminal runs
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/workers/live-snapshots.ts:145-153` - isTerminalRun logic
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:658` - bridge fetch with 5s timeout
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:42-44` - polling intervals (15s refresh, 150ms grace)

**Problem B (Window sliding):**
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/WorkerEntriesManager.ts:118` - DEFAULT_TAIL_LIMIT = 100
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/WorkerEntriesManager.ts:279-280` - tail slice on cache load
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/WorkerEntriesManager.ts:565-603` - fetchForward and entry window management
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/interface/home/worker-elicitations.ts:90-115` - derivePendingElicitationsFromWorkerEntries depends on entries array
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/home/ConversationMain.tsx:54-55` - refresh intervals (2s active, 5s validation)
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/home/ConversationMain.tsx:901-909` - pendingElicitations combo source

**Rendering:**
- `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/home/ConversationMain.tsx:1136-1144` - conditional InlineElicitation render

The bug is a **race between a fast 2-second worker stream window-sliding cycle and a slower 5-15 second agent snapshot refresh**, where the elicitation entry scrolls out of the 100-entry window before the next agent snapshot arrives to repopulate the combined list.

parent: a0940690-66a7-43d0-886e-10a8eac057b3
````

```text
      await syncConversationSessions(rawAgents, {

      records = await readPersistedEventRecords(options);

      scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
      workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
      probe?.mark(`workerSeqs#2[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);
      agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:16:23.399Z

I found the flicker issue—it's happening server-side in the SSE loop. Each cycle starts building the enriched event payload with live pending elicitations, but races it against a 150ms timeout. When the payload doesn't finish in time, it falls back to sending the persisted version instead.

The persisted payload doesn't include the live agent data (no pending elicitations), so the form disappears. Then when the enriched payload finally arrives ~4-5 seconds later, the form reappears. Since the loop keeps spinning whenever event stream notifications arrive (which happens constantly during agent output), it keeps sending the persisted payload first, then the enriched one—creating that repeating gone-then-back flicker pattern.

This same fast-spinning loop also explains the typing lag: every time an agent produces output anywhere, the server rebuilds and pushes a full snapshot payload continuously, triggering full client re-renders. I need to check whether `waitForEventStreamNotification` is global or scoped, which would explain why the lag happens even across different sessions.

```text
function isAgentActive(state: string | null | undefined) {

}

  return (run?.status ?? "").trim().toLowerCase() === "failed";
}

function isTerminalRun(run: PersistedRunRecord | null) {
  const status = (run?.status ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
  return status === "done"
    || status === "failed"
    || status === "cancelled"
    || status === "canceled"
    || status === "promoting"
    || status === "promoted";
}

function shouldSurfaceBridgeLastError(agent: AgentRecord) {
  if (!agent.lastError) {
    return false;
  }

  if (agent.state === "error") {
    return true;
  }

  if (isAgentActive(agent.state)) {
    return false;
  }

  return !agent.currentText.trim() && !agent.lastText.trim() && (agent.outputEntries?.length ?? 0) === 0;
}
```

I've identified the root cause: when the enriched build takes longer than 150ms during an SSE cycle, the server sends a payload with missing agent elicitations and permissions data, then the complete payload arrives a few seconds later. I'm now verifying the logic in the bridgeMissing branch to understand how this gap occurs.

Looking at the client-side handling, there's already a `snapshotSource` concept in EventStreamStateManager that distinguishes between persisted and runtime payloads — I can extend this existing mechanism to handle the timing mismatch rather than building something new.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:17:00.403Z

So the issue is confirmed: `bridgeMissing` is true with no pending elicitations. For the fix, I'm considering a server-side approach where we avoid sending the persisted fallback payload as a full replacement when an enriched payload is already in transit. The 150ms grace period gets something to the client quickly on the first cycle, but on subsequent cycles the client already has state, so pushing a degraded snapshot followed by the enriched version creates unnecessary churn.

The best approach is to use the persisted fast-path only on the initial iteration, then always wait for the runtime-enriched payload afterward. This eliminates flicker across all fields. I could also add a client-side guard: since persisted payloads are already marked with `bridgeMissing: true`, the client could preserve previous live agent fields when receiving a degraded snapshot after having a non-degraded one. Combining both strategies—server-side: skip the degraded frame after the first cycle; client-side: retain live-only fields when merging degraded snapshots—would be the most robust solution, though I need to be careful about how client-side retention interacts with the update logic.

The key insight is distinguishing between a fast-path persisted frame (bridge not yet fetched) versus an actual bridge failure. Adding a payload-level flag like `agentsLive: boolean` would let the server mark persisted payloads as `false` and runtime-enriched ones as `true`, then the client could preserve the previous agents array when applying an update with `agentsLive === false` instead of overwriting with stale data.

Actually, there's a simpler server-side fix that avoids protocol changes entirely: just don't send the persisted fallback frame if we've already sent a runtime-enriched frame on this connection. That's a minimal change in the SSE loop that eliminates the flicker. Let me check if the client already gets an initial snapshot from the bootstrap endpoint, which would make the fast path even less necessary.

Now I'm looking at the second issue around typing lag, which stems from the same loop spinning. Let me look at the live-updates.ts file to see if there's any throttling or batching mechanism in place.

```text
    });

      type: "worker_idle",

      updatesActivity: false,
    });
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:17:22.041Z

So the real bottleneck is that every SSE update triggers a massive synchronous operation: reading up to 4MB from localStorage, parsing it, compacting the entire state across all agents and output entries, stringifying everything back, and then writing it all back to disk synchronously. This is happening on every single state change during streaming, which is absolutely crushing the main thread.

Now I need to check whether the composer draft goes through the same manager — if keystrokes also trigger this 4MB localStorage cycle, that would explain the typing lag even outside the session.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:18:04.945Z

The composer text updates through `homeUiStateManager` on each keystroke, triggering re-renders across the entire HomeApp tree since it subscribes to both that state and the event stream. But the real performance culprit is the localStorage churn that correlates with agent output. I've got solid evidence pointing to both root causes now and can lay out a concrete fix.

The user wants this fixed, so I'll implement. The first issue is the elicitation flicker — the SSE loop takes a fast-path every 150ms that sends a degraded payload with all agents marked as `bridgeMissing: true` and empty elicitations/permissions arrays, then the enriched payload arrives seconds later. This repeats continuously while an agent streams, creating that 1-second-on/4-5-second-off cycle. The fix is to skip the degraded fast-path until the first enriched payload has been delivered on the connection, then always wait for the full enriched payload instead.

I'm implementing a flag that tracks whether we've sent a runtime-enriched payload yet. On the first iteration, we race the enriched payload against a grace timer — if the timer wins, we send the degraded payload and then wait for the enriched one. After that first enriched payload arrives, we always wait for the enriched payload without the race condition.

For the second fix, I'm adding client-side defense so that even if a degraded frame slips through (bridge fetch failure or `bridgeMissing: true`), we preserve the user's pending elicitations and permissions from the previous snapshot instead of wiping them out.

The key invariant is that a snapshot with no live agent data should never claim there's no pending human input. I should enforce this server-side in the `buildLiveWorkerSnapshot` function's degraded branch.

But actually, the client-side merge is where this needs to happen — when `state.agents` gets replaced wholesale during updates, I need to add a merge step that preserves human-input state from the previous agents rather than losing it. This means creating a `mergeAgentHumanInput` function to handle that transition properly.

Now I'm looking at a performance issue with localStorage churn. The snapshot cache manager is synchronously reading and writing to localStorage on every update, which involves parsing the full state, compacting it, and serializing it back — this is becoming a bottleneck on mobile.

I can fix this by keeping an in-memory envelope so reads don't require parsing every time, and by coalescing writes using `requestIdleCallback` or `setTimeout` with a minimum interval and a trailing flush on page visibility changes. The same optimization applies to the worker entries manager. Plus, fixing the double-frame issue should already cut the frame rate impact roughly in half, and I should add a floor to the SSE loop so constant notifications don't trigger snapshot rebuilds too frequently. I should check the test setup and write regression tests since the project has solid test coverage. Let me look at the AGENTS.md file to understand the conventions.

Do NOT add a parallel persistence layer (a sibling JSONL, a new `messages.kind`, an in-memory cache that the frontend reconciles against the stream). See `docs/architecture/worker-conversation-stream.md`.

```text
Lifecycle observability rules (full doc: `docs/architecture/lifecycle-observability-and-testing.md`):
- Every server-side decision (spawn, reattach, recreate, give up, refuse, delete, fail) emits a typed named event via `emitNamedEvent` from `@/server/events/named-events`. Silent early returns and bare `catch {}` are bugs.
- User-relevant failures additionally emit `error.surfaced` with a stable `code` (typed union in `named-events.ts`), `surface`, and at least one relevant subject id such as `runId`/`workerId`/`conversationId`/`accountId`. Never funnel through a blanket wrapper in `api-errors.ts`.
- All SSE frames carry an `id:`. Clients reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; the server replays from the ring buffer or emits `stream.resync_required`. Snapshot bootstrap is `GET /api/events?snapshot=1` (anchor id in the `x-omni-last-event-id` response header).
- Dev-only event log: `GET /api/events/log?since=<id>&runId=<id>` returns the ring buffer as JSON. Use this when triaging "X didn't happen" bug reports — if the event isn't there, the server didn't do the thing, and the next step is finding the silent branch.
- Chaos is a client-side concern. Never add fault-injection code paths to server code.

Frontend i18n:
- EVERY user-facing frontend string MUST live in `shared/locales/*.json` and be rendered with the `t()` function from `@/lib/i18n`.
- NEVER hardcode user-facing JSX text, button labels, dialog titles, aria-labels, titles, placeholders, empty states, status labels, help text, error fallback text, or visible option labels directly in components.
- For every new user-facing string, add the key to `shared/locales/en.json` and every other locale file in `shared/locales/` in the same change. Use stable dotted keys like `settings.runtime.recovery` or `conversation.sidebar.search`.
- Components that render translated strings and need to update when the language changes MUST subscribe to the i18n manager by calling `useI18nSnapshot()` from `@/lib/i18n`; then render text with the existing `t("key", params?)` function. The hook is only for re-rendering; `t()` is the translation API.
- Non-React modules that produce user-visible text must still use `t("key", params?)` at the boundary where text is produced. Protocol values, storage keys, API paths, CSS classes, model ids, and database values are not translation keys unless they are displayed as copy.
- Do not pass translated strings through transactions or persist translated UI copy. Store stable ids/values and translate at render time.

React Best Practices:
- MutableRefObject is deprecated in React; use RefObject instead.
- NEVER use require() to import modules. Use import instead.
- ALWAYS centralize all state in global single source of truth Manager classes. Components/listeners subscribe to updates from Managers and use Manager methods to update data.
- Always implement a custom data manager for any data structure. NEVER use separate state variables and arrays as the source of truth.
- NEVER send data around in transactions.
- Avoid using useEffect() to update state. Prefer useCallback() or Manager methods for explicit state transitions.
- Avoid callback hell, race conditions, and infinite loops.
- NEVER store string literals or UI settings for the frontend in the .env file. Use literals in files, inline arrays, or .json files instead.
- When debugging React: if a fix did not work, think hard about whether this is a race condition. Race conditions are common in React.
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:19:19.328Z

The key insight is keeping the in-memory envelope as the source of truth for reads while deferring only the actual storage write. This way, tests that call `rememberState` and immediately read through `getCachedState` still work synchronously since `readEnvelope` returns the in-memory copy when it exists. The design separates the serialization and storage operation from the cache's internal state management.

I'm also realizing I should defer the compaction step itself — instead of compacting on every `rememberState` call, I'll store the raw state reference in memory and only compact it when flushing to storage. So `rememberState` just tracks pending states and schedules a flush, while `readEnvelope` and `getCachedState` read from the in-memory envelope with uncompacted state, and the actual compaction happens at serialization time.

For the flush-on-hide behavior, I'll register the `pagehide` and `visibilitychange` listeners directly in the constructor, guarded by a check for the default storage option — that way it only activates when using real browser storage, not in tests with memory storage. I also need to capture the current timestamp at `rememberState` time for proper ordering, and handle envelope pruning at write time during the flush.

Now I'm ready to implement the new EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager.

```text
type WorkerEntryStorage = Pick<Storage, "getItem" | "setItem" | "removeItem">;

const DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY = "omni-worker-entries-cache:v1";
const DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS = 16;
const DEFAULT_MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES = 4_000_000;
const DEFAULT_TAIL_LIMIT = 100;
const DEFAULT_OLDER_LIMIT = 100;

interface CachedWorkerStream {
  updatedAt: number;
  entries: WorkerEntry[];
}

interface WorkerEntriesCacheEnvelope {
  version: 1;
  workers: Record<string, CachedWorkerStream>;
}

export type WorkerStreamStatus = "idle" | "loading" | "loaded" | "error";

export interface WorkerStreamState {
  workerId: string;
  entries: WorkerEntry[];
  lowestSeq: number;
  latestContiguousSeq: number;
  latestKnownSeq: number;
  hasOlder: boolean;
  status: WorkerStreamStatus;
  lastError: string | null;
  needsTailValidation?: boolean;
}

type Listener = (state: WorkerStreamState) => void;

interface FetchResponse {
  entries: WorkerEntry[];
  latestSeq: number;
  hasOlder?: boolean;
}

export interface WorkerEntriesManagerOptions {
  listEntries?: RuntimeAPIs["workers"]["listEntries"];
  storage?: WorkerEntryStorage | null;
  storageKey?: string;
  maxWorkers?: number;
  maxSerializedBytes?: number;
  now?: () => number;
}

function latestSeq(entries: WorkerEntry[]) {
  return entries.reduce((latest, entry) => (
    typeof entry.seq === "number" && Number.isFinite(entry.seq)
      ? Math.max(latest, entry.seq)
      : latest
  ), 0);
}

function initialState(
  workerId: string,
  entries: WorkerEntry[] = [],
  options: { needsTailValidation?: boolean } = {},
): WorkerStreamState {
  const latest = latestSeq(entries);
  const lowest = entries.length > 0
    ? entries.reduce((acc, entry) => (
      typeof entry.seq === "number" && entry.seq > 0 && (acc === 0 || entry.seq < acc) ? entry.seq : acc
    ), 0)
    : 0;
  return {
    workerId,
    entries,
    lowestSeq: lowest,
    latestContiguousSeq: latest,
    latestKnownSeq: latest,
    hasOlder: lowest > 1,
    status: entries.length > 0 ? "loaded" : "idle",
    lastError: null,
    needsTailValidation: options.needsTailValidation,
  };
}

function defaultStorage(): WorkerEntryStorage | null {
  if (typeof window === "undefined" || typeof window.localStorage === "undefined") {
    return null;
  }
  return window.localStorage;
}

function emptyEnvelope(): WorkerEntriesCacheEnvelope {
  return {
    version: 1,
    workers: {},
  };
}

function isWorkerEntryArray(value: unknown): value is WorkerEntry[] {
  return Array.isArray(value) && value.every((entry) => (
    typeof entry === "object"
    && entry !== null
    && typeof (entry as Partial<WorkerEntry>).id === "string"
    && typeof (entry as Partial<WorkerEntry>).seq === "number"
  ));
}
```

```text
  private readEnvelope(): WorkerEntriesCacheEnvelope {
    if (!this.storage) {
      return emptyEnvelope();
    }

    try {
      const raw = this.storage.getItem(this.storageKey);
      if (!raw) {
        return emptyEnvelope();
      }

      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<WorkerEntriesCacheEnvelope>;
      if (parsed.version !== 1 || typeof parsed.workers !== "object" || parsed.workers === null) {
        return emptyEnvelope();
      }
      return {
        version: 1,
        workers: parsed.workers as Record<string, CachedWorkerStream>,
      };
    } catch {
      try {
        this.storage.removeItem(this.storageKey);
      } catch {
        // Ignore cleanup failures.
      }
      return emptyEnvelope();
    }
  }

  private pruneEnvelope(envelope: WorkerEntriesCacheEnvelope): WorkerEntriesCacheEnvelope {
    return {
      version: 1,
      workers: Object.fromEntries(
        Object.entries(envelope.workers)
          .sort((left, right) => {
            const updatedDelta = right[1].updatedAt - left[1].updatedAt;
            return updatedDelta !== 0 ? updatedDelta : left[0].localeCompare(right[0]);
          })
          .slice(0, this.maxWorkers),
      ),
    };
  }
}

// A single process-wide instance is fine because manager state is keyed
// by workerId and the same worker is never owned by two tabs. The
// reset() method exists for tests; production code should not call it.
export const workerEntriesManager = new WorkerEntriesManager();

 * from the manager's contiguous-prefix invariant.
 *
 * `workerId === null` returns a stable empty state and skips the
 * fetch.
 */
interface UseWorkerStreamOptions {
  refreshIntervalMs?: number | null;
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:21:16.823Z

I'm seeing two test failures where a second manager instance should read entries cached by the first, but with deferred flushing the data never gets written to storage in time. These tests are actually testing a legitimate scenario—like a page reload—where persistence across instances matters. The issue is that real page reloads trigger a flush via pagehide, but the tests don't have that mechanism, so I need to figure out whether to modify the tests with `flushIntervalMs: 0` or find a better approach that doesn't change the test behavior itself.

The cleanest solution is to have the tests explicitly call `flushCache()` on the first manager before creating the second one. That way the test clearly documents what it's checking—that after the cache is persisted, a fresh manager can read it—without weakening the test or changing the default behavior.

```text
/**
 * Reads SSE chunks until an `event: update` frame arrives and returns
 * its parsed JSON payload. Use this in tests that previously relied on
 * "the first chunk contains the snapshot" — named events now interleave
 * with snapshots on the wire.
 */
async function readUntilUpdateFrame(
  reader: ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>,
  timeoutMs = 4_000,
  predicate?: (payload: Record<string, unknown>) => boolean,
): Promise<any> {
  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
  let buffer = "";
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const readResult = await Promise.race([
      reader.read(),
      new Promise<{ value?: Uint8Array; done?: boolean }>((resolve) =>
        setTimeout(() => resolve({ value: undefined, done: false }), 200),
      ),
    ]);
    if (readResult.done) {
      throw new Error("SSE stream closed without an update frame");
    }
    if (!readResult.value) continue;
    buffer += decoder.decode(readResult.value, { stream: true });
    const frames = buffer.split("\n\n");
    buffer = frames.pop() ?? "";
    for (const frame of frames) {
      const lines = frame.split("\n");
      const eventLine = lines.find((line) => line.startsWith("event: "));
      if (eventLine?.slice("event: ".length) !== "update") continue;
      const dataLine = lines.find((line) => line.startsWith("data: "));
      if (dataLine) {
        const payload = JSON.parse(dataLine.slice("data: ".length)) as Record<string, unknown>;
        if (!predicate || predicate(payload)) {
          return payload;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  throw new Error(`Timed out waiting ${timeoutMs}ms for an update frame`);
}

async function readWithTimeout(reader: ReadableStreamDefaultReader<Uint8Array>, timeoutMs: number) {
  let timeoutId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
  const timeout = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
    timeoutId = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Timed out waiting ${timeoutMs}ms for SSE update`)), timeoutMs);
  });

  try {
    return await Promise.race([reader.read(), timeout]);
  } finally {
    if (timeoutId) {
      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    }
  }
}

function mockAgentRuntimeJson(payload: unknown, init?: ResponseInit) {
  global.fetch = vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => Promise.resolve(
    new Response(JSON.stringify(payload), init),
  ));
}
```

I need to write a regression test that verifies a runtime-enriched frame isn't followed by a degraded persisted frame during a slow subsequent build. Then I'll trigger another loop iteration by calling `notifyEventStreamSubscribers()` from the live-updates module, advance the fake timers past the grace window, and assert that no update frame with `bridgeMissing: true` or empty pending elicitations appears—confirming the loop is still awaiting the enriched payload rather than falling back to a persisted frame.

I should also verify that `shareInFlightEventPayload` properly rebuilds its cache on the second call after notification, since it dedupes by version and the enriched payload will differ from the persisted one.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:25:18.867Z

The lifecycle tests are passing, which is good. Looking at the typing lag issue more carefully, the localStorage operations were causing the most significant main-thread blocking, but there's also the SSE stream continuously sending full payloads as the agent generates output. With the first fix in place, the server now sends a single frame per rebuild instead of alternating between degraded and enriched states, which should cut the frame volume in half and eliminate the churn from those state transitions.

That alternation was particularly problematic because every agent object was changing on each frame, preventing React from maintaining reference stability and forcing maximum re-render work. The supervisor observer fires notifications at several points during output generation, so I'm checking whether the loop has any natural throttling. With the fix, each iteration waits for the full enriched build to complete, which takes multiple seconds, so the frame rate is naturally constrained by that build duration rather than spinning freely. This should be a meaningful improvement, though I'm considering whether additional coalescing on the notification side would help further.

Actually, I'm reconsidering the localStorage fix: `compactStateForCache` now runs at flush time across all scopes instead of per-write, which is more work per flush but flushes happen at most once per second instead of many times per second—a net win. One thing to verify though: the in-memory envelope in `EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager` now holds uncompacted state including raw output entries and frontend errors, whereas previously hydration would get compacted states from storage. Within a session, hydration might now receive uncompacted data, which is more data but not a correctness issue. I'm also holding up to eight full states in memory, which increases retention slightly for old scopes but these are references to states we already maintain.

I should do a final review of the diff and verify the app still builds.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:25:45.412Z

There's an edge case where if the bridge goes down permanently, the error gets caught and the payload is built with a `bridgeError` flag instead, so it still resolves with agents marked as `bridgeMissing: true`. The fetch has a 5-second timeout, so `hasDeliveredRuntimePayload` becomes true from that path as well, and future iterations wait on it (capped at 5s). This prevents hangs while still surfacing the degraded state when the bridge is actually unavailable.

When the bridge is genuinely down, the enriched payload has `bridgeMissing: true`, and my client-side merge logic preserves the last-known pending elicitations indefinitely — which is the right call. If the bridge is dead, those elicitations can't be answered anyway, and keeping them visible along with the `bridgeLastError` signal is more informative than clearing them silently. Once the bridge recovers, the live frame clears it. This aligns with the "fix forever" property the user wanted: a form being filled can't be yanked away by a frame that doesn't actually know what's happening.

I should probably write up a learnings doc in the docs/superpowers/learnings/ folder. The `learning-from-bugs` skill exists and this bug diagnosis and fix qualifies for it, though I'll mention it rather than auto-invoke.

One honest limitation: I couldn't reproduce this on an actual mobile device, so my verification relies on unit and integration tests rather than a live mobile session. Let me also double-check that the elicitation flicker fix handles the case where `primaryConversationAgent` is null entirely in the degraded frame — meaning the agent disappears from `state.agents`. In the persisted payload, `buildLiveWorkerSnapshots` iterates workers and creates a snapshot for each, so the agent entry still exists with `bridgeMissing` set. My merge logic matches by name and finds it. Both the persisted and live paths use the same `selectedRunWorkers` function, so they're working with the same set of workers. Now I need to verify whether `mergeDegradedAgentHumanInput` runs for cache-source updates.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:26:00.173Z

The optimistic update bypasses the merge logic, so clearing an elicitation happens immediately without resurrecting it. Then when the degraded server frame arrives, the merge checks `current.agents` where `pendingElicitations` is already empty from the optimistic clear, so the merge can't restore what's no longer there.

But there's a deeper issue: if the current agent state is degraded and holds a preserved elicitation, then another degraded frame comes in, my condition checks `currentAgent.bridgeMissing` — which is true — and returns the incoming agent unchanged, dropping the preserved value. That reintroduces the flicker on consecutive degraded frames.

The real fix is to preserve as long as the current agent has pending items, regardless of whether it's marked as degraded. The `bridgeMissing` guard doesn't actually protect anything useful. I should remove it and rely on the live frame or optimistic local update as the only clearing paths, then add a test case for this scenario.

## Claude · 2026-08-03T17:27:05.956Z

Both bugs traced to one chain and fixed. All tests green (`tests/app`, `tests/api`, `tests/ui`, `tests/interface`, `tests/server`, `pnpm test:lifecycle`), typecheck clean.

## Bug 1: the flickering form

Not mobile-specific — mobile just made it obvious. It's in the SSE loop at `src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:964`.

Each iteration kicks off the runtime-enriched payload (which fetches the bridge for live agent state) and races it against a **150ms** grace timer. If the build isn't done in 150ms, the server sends the **persisted** payload first. That payload is built with no `agents` argument (`events.ts:574`), so every agent goes down the bridge-missing branch and gets `pendingElicitations: []`, `pendingPermissions: []` hardcoded (`src/server/workers/live-snapshots.ts:270-271`).

So every cycle the client got: **degraded frame** (form gone) → *seconds later* **enriched frame** (form back). And because `waitForEventStreamNotification` returns instantly while an agent is producing output, the loop never parked — it span continuously. Form visible for the moment the enriched frame was current, gone for the whole multi-second rebuild. Exactly your 1s-on / 4-5s-off.

Two fixes, so it can't come back:
- **`events.ts`** — the degraded fast path is now only allowed before the first live frame (good first paint, no replay after).
- **`EventStreamStateManager.ts`** — a new `mergeDegradedAgentHumanInput` enforces the invariant that a snapshot which *couldn't reach the runtime* may not assert "nothing is pending". Only a frame that actually talked to the runtime, or the local optimistic update from the answer path, can clear a pending request.

While writing the test I caught a gap in my own first cut: I'd gated the merge on `currentAgent.bridgeMissing`, which meant two *consecutive* degraded frames would still drop the form. Removed, with a test covering it.

## Bug 2: the typing lag

Related, and this one is the direct cause. On **every** event-stream update, `EventStreamSnapshotCacheManager.rememberState` synchronously did: `localStorage.getItem` (up to 4MB) → `JSON.parse` → map every agent and its output entries → `JSON.stringify` → `localStorage.setItem`. `WorkerEntriesManager.rememberState` did the same on every append and every 2s poll.

`localStorage` is synchronous and blocks the main thread. When any agent anywhere streams output, notifications are global and unthrottled, so this ran many times a second — starving keystroke handling. Different session doesn't matter; the notification and the cache envelope are both global.

Both now keep the envelope in memory (reads unchanged, writes O(1)) and coalesce the serialize+write onto a trailing 1s timer, flushed on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` so a backgrounded PWA doesn't lose it. Fix 1 also cuts frame count roughly in half and, more importantly, stops every frame from flipping every agent object between degraded and live — which was defeating memoization downstream.

## Regression tests

I verified each fails without its fix rather than assuming:
- `tests/api/events-route.test.ts` — no degraded frame after live state has streamed. Fails with the gate removed.
- `tests/app/event-stream-state-manager.test.ts` — 3 tests: degraded frames preserve pending input (incl. consecutive), live frames still clear it, optimistic answer isn't resurrected. Verified failing without the merge.

Two caveats worth stating plainly: three `tests/server/agent-runtime` failures exist, but they're pre-existing — I confirmed by stashing my changes and re-running. And I validated this through tests, not a live mobile PWA session, so it's worth a quick confirm on your phone next time an agent asks a question.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:38:07.709Z

All tests are passing now with the pre-existing failures resolved. For the performance work, I need to verify the claims about client-side rendering issues before diving into fixes—specifically checking whether HomeApp's unfiltered subscription to the event stream is causing unnecessary re-renders on every frame, whether SSE frames are being batched, and investigating the third issue that got cut off.

Looking at the code, HomeApp does subscribe to the full state object without a selector, which means every update triggers a re-render of the entire tree. While HomeApp legitimately needs most of that state, the real bottleneck for typing lag isn't the composer textarea itself—re-rendering that with the same value is relatively cheap. The expensive part is the rest of the tree (transcript, Terminal) re-rendering on every frame and blocking the main thread, which delays keystroke handling. So the highest-impact fix would be memoizing those expensive subtrees, particularly the Terminal component.

But before diving into that refactor with its regression risk, I should verify whether the localStorage optimization I already made was actually the dominant cost, and measure what's left to address.

```text
=== impl ===
"use client";

import { useCallback, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import type { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";

export function useManagerSnapshot<TState>(manager: StateManager<TState>) {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
    useCallback(() => manager.getSnapshot(), [manager]),
    useCallback(() => manager.getInitialSnapshot(), [manager]),
  );
}

export function shallowEqualRecord<TRecord extends Record<string, unknown>>(
  left: TRecord,
  right: TRecord,
) {
  if (Object.is(left, right)) {
    return true;
  }

  const leftKeys = Object.keys(left);
  const rightKeys = Object.keys(right);
  if (leftKeys.length !== rightKeys.length) {
    return false;
  }

  return leftKeys.every((key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(right, key)
    && Object.is(left[key], right[key]));
}

export function useManagerSelector<TState, TSelected>(
  manager: StateManager<TState>,
  selector: (state: TState) => TSelected,
  isEqual: (left: TSelected, right: TSelected) => boolean = Object.is,
) {
  const selectionRef = useRef<{
    state: TState;
    selection: TSelected;
  } | null>(null);
  const serverSelectionRef = useRef<{
    state: TState;
    selector: (state: TState) => TSelected;
    selection: TSelected;
  } | null>(null);

  const getSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
    const state = manager.getSnapshot();
    const previous = selectionRef.current;
    if (previous?.state === state) {
      return previous.selection;
    }

    const nextSelection = selector(state);
    if (previous && isEqual(previous.selection, nextSelection)) {
      selectionRef.current = {
        state,
        selection: previous.selection,
      };
      return previous.selection;
    }

    selectionRef.current = {
      state,
      selection: nextSelection,
    };
    return nextSelection;
  }, [isEqual, manager, selector]);
  const getServerSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
    const state = manager.getInitialSnapshot();
    const previous = serverSelectionRef.current;
    if (previous?.state === state && previous.selector === selector) {
      return previous.selection;
    }
    const selection = selector(state);
    serverSelectionRef.current = { state, selector, selection };
    return selection;
  }, [manager, selector]);

  return useSyncExternalStore(
    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
    getSelectedSnapshot,
    getServerSelectedSnapshot,
  );
}
```

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-03T17:38:47.760Z

The benchmark shows the old approach takes about 3.9ms per update on this M-series Mac, which translates to roughly 31ms of main thread time per second at 8 frames—noticeable but not severe. However, the real bottleneck isn't the JSON processing itself; it's the actual `localStorage.setItem` call, which performs a synchronous disk write of the 3.5MB string, and on mobile browsers especially this becomes the dominant cost and significantly slower than the computation work.

My measurement only captures the serialization component—around 4ms per frame on a fast desktop, scaling to 12-20ms on mobile CPUs—but doesn't account for the actual localStorage I/O, which on mobile Chrome can add 50-200ms or more. Since there were two such caches involved, that's effectively doubling the impact. Now I need to look at Terminal's per-render cost since it's unmemoized and the largest component, particularly examining what `buildAgentOutputActivity` does and whether the entries identity remains stable across renders.
